proposals.impact: lift open rate on Money Worship from 37.5% toward Money Vigilance's 66.67% by studying what the subject line is doing differently
proposals.observation: Money Vigilance automation opened at 66.67% (8 of 12). Money Worship opened at 37.5% (6 of 16). That is a 29-percentage-point gap across sequences that likely share a subscriber pool. The difference almost certainly lives in the subject line or preview text of email 01 in each sequence, not in the body copy. Money Vigilance subscribers are the ones who check every penny and feel quietly ashamed of it — Joel's subject line for that sequence is probably more specific and more recognisably their internal voice. Money Worship subscribers tend to use spending to feel okay, which is a harder internal state to name without sounding judgemental. The subject line for that sequence is probably too broad to feel personal.
proposals.proposal: Pull the subject line and preview text from Money Vigilance email 01 and compare it directly against Money Worship email 01. Rewrite the Money Worship subject line so it names the specific internal experience — not the behaviour, but what the person feels in the moment before the behaviour. The gym-bag moment is the model: not "you overspend" but "you bought the thing and immediately felt the same as before." That specificity is what makes someone open rather than archive. Change only the subject and preview_text frontmatter fields in email-01.md for the Money Worship sequence. Do not touch body copy.

proposals.impact: restore automated daily publishing — currently zero posts queued after the 05:36 failure
proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 05:36 on 2026-07-18. There is one post in the queue and zero published in the last 24 hours. The content queue shows 47 published posts and only 1 queued, so the failure is not a content shortage — it is a workflow execution problem. With the quiz also at zero sessions, the blog is the only organic entry point currently running, and it is not running.
proposals.proposal: Open the daily-blog-post workflow file and check the failure point. The most common causes for this class of CI failure in Astro-based static sites are: a missing or rotated API secret, a changed branch name, or a build step that depends on a node version that drifted. Add an explicit `on: workflow_dispatch` trigger if it is not already present so Joel can manually re-run from the GitHub Actions UI without waiting for the next scheduled cron. Also add a `continue-on-error: false` line to the publish step so failures surface clearly rather than silently skipping. This is a two-line addition that restores manual control today while the root cause is diagnosed.

proposals.impact: zero quiz sessions in 48h means no new leads entering any automation — adding a visible entry-point CTA recovers the top of the funnel
proposals.observation: The quiz shows zero sessions and zero starts across a 48-hour window. All three active automations — Money Avoidance, Money Worship, Money Vigilance — depend on the quiz as their intake mechanism. Without quiz completions, no new subscribers enter any sequence, and the list stops growing. The recent blog posts (course-buying compulsion, goal avoidance, comparison to peers) are exactly the content that the ICP reads at the moment they are most ready to self-identify. If those posts do not carry a visible, in-body CTA pointing to the quiz, readers are arriving and leaving without a next step.
proposals.proposal: Add a short in-body CTA block to the most recent blog post — the course-buying one published 2026-06-07 — pointing readers to the quiz. Place it after the second or third paragraph, not at the end, because readers who reach the end are already converted or already gone. The CTA should name the specific thing the quiz does — identify which money pattern is running the show — rather than making a generic promise. Write it in Joel's register: grounded, direct, no performance. One paragraph, no heading, no bullet list.
proposals.new_text: If that pattern sounds familiar — buying the thing, feeling briefly hopeful, then returning to exactly the same place — it is worth knowing which money script is underneath it. Joel built a short quiz that identifies your dominant pattern from four distinct types. It takes about four minutes. The results tell you something specific, not a personality label.
